change_summary: The journal has retracted the paper. An institutional investigation found that the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated, and the notice says the conclusions cannot be relied on. The paper's Results section cites Figures 2 to 4 for its accuracy result at 200 mg. The authors have not responded.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] for the finding that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, and uses it as the reason for choosing your 200 mg dose. The stored paper reports that 12% result in its Section 3.2, and the journal has retracted the paper because the data in Figures 2 to 4 were found fabricated. The notice says the conclusions cannot be relied on. The justification for your dose choice therefore rests on a retracted finding, so this matters a lot. This is the only place your draft cites it.
recommendation: Remove or replace the Brown and Kim [3] citation in your Introduction and re-check your 200 mg dose rationale. Your draft cites it for the 12% improvement at 200 mg, and the journal has retracted the paper because an institutional investigation found fabricated data in Figures 2 to 4.
